title: OLD-biased-vs-CORRECTED GLMM comparison for fig05: model D (defensible within-subject V3-vs-V1V2, session-level) flips beta band from null (p_bh=0.381) to nominally significant (p_bh=0.019) after the P0 dB-averaging fix; model A (corpus-wide) stays null in both but SEs inflate 4-5x
notes: Ran scripts/compute_channel_band_power_census_v2.py against the full 22-session/970-file TFR corpus (outputs/lfp_band_census_v2/channel_band_power.csv.gz, 404,595 rows, receipt confirms n_files_omission_processed=873, n_files_skipped=0), then refit scripts/fit_omission_band_power_glmm.py against it. This is the corrected estimator per fig05-p0-dB-averaging-fix-20260811 (power averaged over trials first, log taken once), run for the first time at full-corpus scale -- prior runs this sprint were 4- and 10-file smoke tests.

COMPARISON TABLE at outputs/lfp_band_census_v2/old_vs_corrected_comparison.csv (115 rows, all models A/B/C/D, both channel- and session-level variants). OLD baseline is the pre-fix Aug 5 2026 run (glmm_pre_fullcorpus_20260805/, byte-identical to the old_biased_20260811/ smoke-test snapshot), which used a different, larger corpus at the time (n_sessions=23 in model A vs 22 now -- the corpus has been revised multiple times across this project's history, 23 predates even the 21-session state this sprint's handoff describes; not a discrepancy introduced by this task, noted for the record rather than reconciled).

MODEL A (corpus-wide, db ~ 1 + (1|session/probe)): null in every band before AND after the fix (all p_bh > 0.05, all p_bh_CORRECTED > 0.89 in fact). No sign flip. BUT the standard errors on the intercept inflated roughly 4-5x after the fix (e.g. theta se 0.145 -> 0.759, beta se 0.0997 -> 0.589). Interpretation: the previous per-trial dB-averaging estimator likely shrank between-channel/between-session variance via the same Jensen's-inequality mechanism that biased its point estimate (documented in db_averaging_bias_finding_20260728) -- this is consistent with, not contradictory to, that prior finding, and is offered as inference, not independently re-derived here.

MODEL D, CHANNEL-LEVEL (the raw C(probe_group)[T.V3] rows): both OLD and CORRECTED show astronomically small p-values (down to 1e-202) in every band. THESE ARE NOT TRUSTWORTHY -- the script's own inline comment (fit_omission_band_power_glmm.py, preceding the session-level companion models) states this level 'implausibly' anti-conservative because channels within a probe are strongly dependent, with |z| routinely above 40 on a sub-dB effect. Do not cite the channel-level D numbers as evidence of anything; they are reported here only because they are in the same output file.

MODEL D, SESSION-LEVEL (the defensible companion, one obs per session before fitting, n=5 sessions, subject=V198o only -- the only subject/session set where V3-group and V1/V2 sit on separate probes in the same session): theta 0.071->0.544 dB (p_bh 0.812->0.232), alpha 1.163->1.902 dB (p_bh 0.396->0.067), BETA 1.592->2.232 dB (p_bh 0.381 -> 0.019, null to nominally significant), low_gamma 0.563->1.113 dB (p_bh 0.396->0.073), high_gamma -0.166->0.124 dB (p_bh 0.745->0.486). Every band's point estimate moved in the same direction (more positive) after the fix, consistent with the documented bias direction, but only beta crosses the uncorrected-then-BH-corrected 0.05 line.

This is the single result from this sprint's Fig05 work most likely to change what gets reported in the manuscript -- it is based on n=5 sessions, one subject, and the BH correction is across only 5 bands within this one model family (not corrected across the full family of models A-D), so 'nominally significant' is a fair characterization, not 'established'.
issues: n=5 sessions, one subject: this cannot be strengthened without another subject/session set having V3-group and V1/V2 on separate probes in the same session, which per the model's own eligibility check does not currently exist elsewhere in the 22-session corpus.
Not yet decided whether this beta-band result is reported in the manuscript, and if so, how (a single within-subject n=5 contrast is a weak basis for a headline claim even at p_bh=0.019).

The corpus size discrepancy (23 sessions in the OLD run vs 22 now) was not chased down -- flagged, not resolved. If it turns out the OLD run's extra session was a duplicate or QC-excluded session rather than a since-added-then-removed one, the OLD baseline itself may need re-examination, but that does not change the CORRECTED numbers, which are the ones computed from the current, verified 22-session corpus.
plan: Decide whether to report the model-D session-level beta-band result, and if so, draft the Methods/Results caveats (n=5, one subject, uncorrected-for-model-family multiplicity) alongside it.

Decide whether model A's inflated SEs (not the point estimates) need their own sentence in Methods explaining the correction's effect on uncertainty, separate from the point-estimate bias already documented.
Route the corpus session-count discrepancy to whoever owns the historical corpus-revision record, if it becomes relevant.
